newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 18.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 18.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Public Relations, Brand-name Products, Consumer Trends, Media and the Internet
ADVERTISING, MARKETING & PUBLIC RELATIONS:

HAMBURG - Private television stations reported 8.3 percent growth in gross advertising turnover for the first quarter of 1997, the Bauer publishing group says based on figures provided by Nielsen S&P Werbeforschung. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - The main German public relations assocation, the GPRA, says most of its members posted growth in turnover for 1996. It expects further boosts in fee income for the current year. Kothes & Klewes Kommunikation ranked as top PR firm among GPRA members, with 28.4 million marks in fee income, an 18 percent boost from the previous year. (Reuter)

WIESBADEN - The German direct marketing assocation (DDV) says half of the money spent on advertising every year in Germany goes to direct marketing. The industry posted turnover of 30 billion marks for 1996 and predicted 33 billion marks in sales for the current year. (Reuter)

LONDON - Advertising agency M&C Saatchi says it has been awarded a four-million-pound ($6.5 million) UK account by Benckiser, the German household products company. The agency will create a new campaign for Benckiser's Vanish stain removal brand. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - In the court battle between television stations Premiere and DF1, in which Premiere has sought an injunction to block DF1 from advertising or signing contracts with subscribers outside the state of Munich, the Hamburg regional appellate court says it will announce a decision on May 15.(Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Dynewski has gone bankrupt. The company, with offices in Bonn, Berlin, Hamburg and Munich, posted a gross income in 1996 of 8.5 million marks. (Horizont)
MEDIA & INTERNET:

BONN - Germany's Internet industry expects more indictments to follow after Bavarian authorities filed charges against online service CompuServe Inc, marking a decisive turning point in the debate over Internet regulation. Just as the German parliament is set to begin debating legislation that takes a liberal view of policing cyberspace, prosecutors appear to be using CompuServe to set an example meant to urge lawmakers to take a harder line. (Reuter)
BONN - Alarmed over the availability of pornography and extremist writings on the Internet, investigators have set up teams of cybersleuths to surf the Net in search of illicit material. (Reuter)
BONN - Microsoft Network, the U.S. software giant's online service, has shut down its worldwide electronic mail computers until Sunday, customer service officials at the company say.
(Reuter)
COLOGNE - Evosonic Radio GmbH & Co KG says it will start broadcasting on May 1 with an electronic music format. (Handelsblatt)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BONN - The German tobacco industry says it cannot foresee facing liability settlement talks with justice department authorities like its counterparts in the United States. The director of the German cigarette industry association, Ernst rueckner, says German companies are unlikely to confront similar action, largely due to different product liability laws in Germany. (Reuter)
NUREMBERG - Nuremberg-based Sebaldus Druck und Verlag GmbH says it is ready to expand its publishing and printing businesses ince it completed a broad restructuring. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
PEOPLE NEWS:

DUESSELDORF - Advertising agency BBDO Duesseldorf says it has appointed Jan van Meel of the Netherlands as its new executive creative director. Van Meel, who with his team won the Grand Prix in Cannes last year for their Nestle Rollo commercial, was previously the manager of creative development at AP Lintas in Hamburg. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Robert Brandes, auto rental company Hertz's marketing manager for North America, will now also serve as the company's advertising manager for Europe. (Horizont)
DUESSELDORF - Hans Burkhard has joined the board of digital television channel DF1. Burkhard was previously a member of consumer electronics maker Grundig's board. (Handelsblatt)
FRANKFURT - Karl Pohler will take over as managing director of Sony's German unit, Sony Deutschland GmbH. Pohler is currently manager of Computer 2000 Deutschland in Munich. (Horizont)
